findings.title: CurrentBuildingData is a full second copy of the entire factory (~360 B/building) duplicating engine state
findings.mechanism: CartographGameInstanceModule.h:359 declares `TArray<FBuildingData> CurrentBuildingData` holding ONE FBuildingData per world buildable. This duplicates data the engine already stores in AFGBuildableSubsystem::GetAllBuildablesRef() and AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem::mBuildableClassToInstanceArray (the exact sources read at module .cpp:383-388). Precise sizeof(FBuildingData) under UE5.3 LWC (64-bit doubles, 16-byte align) from CartographDataStructure.h:75-109: BuildableClassHash uint32=4; FTransform(LWC)=96 (FQuat4d 32 + FVector3d+pad 32 + Scale3D+pad 32 — note Scale is held in RAM even though NetSerialize at DataStructure.cpp:128-130 deliberately drops it); BuildableExtraData std::variant=24; DataType=4; DataCache std::variant=~176 (dominated by FNormalDataCache: ScreenPosition 16 + Size 16 + FRotator 24 + variant<TSoftObjectPtr~48, FRectangleDataCache 104> where FRectangleDataCache = ptr 8 + FVector Corners[4] 4x24=96); LayerDataCache ptr=8; FBox2D VisualBoxCache=40. Field sum ~356 B, 16-aligned ~360-368 B per building. Totals: 200k buildings = ~72 MB; 1M buildings = ~360 MB of pure duplication. Splines/belts/pipes additionally heap-allocate FSplineExtraData.Points = (SPLINE_SEGMENTS+1)=9 FVector2D = 144 B/spline off-heap (DataStructure.cpp:225-231).
findings.fixDirection: Do not store a parallel array. Iterate the engine's existing buildable arrays on redraw; keep only a compact per-building index (sorted by Z) plus a small POD draw-record (classHash u32 + quantized transform). Drop the in-RAM FTransform Scale3D and FQuat (store a single rotation float + position floats) to shrink the record from ~360 B to ~24-40 B (8-15x reduction).

findings.title: DataCache permanently stores fully precomputed screen-space render data (~176 B/building) that is trivially recomputable on demand
findings.mechanism: FBuildingData.DataCache (DataStructure.h:87) is a std::variant whose dominant member FNormalDataCache (DataStructure.h:60-66) permanently stores ScreenPosition (FVector2D), Size (FVector2D), Rotation (FRotator 24B), and FRectangleDataCache.Corners[4] (4x FVector = 96 B). These are ALL derived purely from Transform + static per-class data (BuildableSizeOverrideMap, BuildCategoryDataMap) via FillInCache (DataStructure.cpp:264-446): ScreenPosition = world_position_to_screen_position(Transform, Size) (line 387), Corners = TransformNoScale.TransformPosition of axis-aligned half-extents (lines 423-433). This is ~176 B of the ~360 B struct (~49%) spent caching values that could be computed in a few FLOPs at draw time. At 1M buildings this is ~176 MB of avoidable resident memory. The cache also forces redundant pointers (LayerDataCache, CategoryData, SplineData/WireData pointers) to be stored per-building when they are per-CLASS.
findings.fixDirection: Recompute screen position, size, corners and rotation inside RedrawMapCoroutine from Transform + a per-CLASS lookup (keyed by classHash) at draw time. Keep only classHash + Z + a 2D bbox for culling. Eliminates FNormalDataCache/FRectangleDataCache storage entirely (~176 B/building saved).

findings.title: 8192x8192 RGBA8 render target costs a fixed 256 MB VRAM regardless of factory size
findings.mechanism: RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE = 1024*8 = 8192 (h:35) and the asset Content/UI/CanvasRenderTarget_BuildingVisualization.uasset is RTF_RGBA8 with SizeX=SizeY=8192 (verified by reading the uasset: keys 'RenderTargetFormat'->'RTF_RGBA8', 'SizeX'->8192, 'SizeY'->8192). VRAM = 8192 x 8192 x 4 bytes = 268,435,456 B = exactly 256 MB, allocated permanently the moment the world loads (cleared at module .cpp:394). This is a flat 256 MB GPU cost that is the prime suspect for the #14 client crash + GPU driver timeout (TDR) after ~1h: a 256 MB committed target plus the full-screen clear+redraw every build event (RedrawMapCoroutine draws a RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE x RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE ClearItem tile each pass, .cpp:653-660) thrashes the GPU. Partial-redraw scissor (CartographCanvasRenderItem ScissorArea) clips raster but the clear tile is still issued full-size.
findings.fixDirection: Reduce to 4096^2 (64 MB, 4x less) or tile the map into on-demand chunks; make size a config option. For partial redraws, restrict the clear tile to ScissorArea bounds instead of the full 8192^2, so the GPU only touches the dirty rect.

findings.title: BuildingDataIndexRedirector never shrinks on removal: stale -1 entries accumulate, plus O(n) churn per build event
findings.mechanism: BuildingDataIndexRedirector (h:365, comment h:361-364 admits it) maps quad-tree node ids to CurrentBuildingData indices. On removal, OnBuildingDataRemove (module .cpp:1213-1234) sets the slot to -1 (line 1224) and decrements higher indices but NEVER calls .RemoveAt/.Shrink. The array is only emptied on full re-gather (.cpp:290,468) or client respawn (.cpp:290). In a long session of build/dismantle (exactly the #14 scenario: repeatedly placing/removing belts for ~1h), the redirector grows by one slot per ADD (OnBuildingDataAdd .cpp:1206 always Add's) and removed slots are never reclaimed, so it grows unbounded toward (total adds over session) x 4 B. Worse, both OnBuildingDataAdd (.cpp:1199-1205) and OnBuildingDataRemove (.cpp:1218-1230) do an O(n) linear scan over the entire redirector on EVERY single building add/remove — so each belt placement is O(buildings), which is a direct contributor to the 15s lag spikes in #14 (memory growth + quadratic CPU compound).
findings.fixDirection: Replace the index-redirector + TQuadTree<int32> with a quad tree keyed by a stable building id (or store FBuildingData* / sparse free-list slot directly), so removal frees the slot and no O(n) reindex is needed. If keeping the array, use a TSparseArray/free-list and compact periodically; never leave permanent -1 tombstones.

findings.title: RCO serializes and holds a full copy of CurrentBuildingData per joining player; client mirrors it again
findings.mechanism: On a dedicated server, ServerRequestInitialBuildingData_Implementation (RCO.cpp:42-55) serializes the ENTIRE CurrentBuildingData into a resizable FBufferWriter (line 48) and stores it in InitialBuildingDataToSendPerPlayer per PlayerController (lines 51-55). The compact NetSerialize (~15-20 B/building, DataStructure.cpp:118-206) yields ~3.6 MB for 200k / ~18 MB for 1M buildings, held in full per concurrent joiner until transfer completes or 10s timeout (lines 83-90). Simultaneously the client accumulates the same bytes in a growing TArray<uint8> Buffer via Buffer.Append per slice (RCO.cpp:97), then deserializes that into ANOTHER full CurrentBuildingData (RCO.cpp:130-147) — so during join the client holds the raw byte buffer AND the rebuilt struct array at once. The freeing path (FMemory::Free at RCO.cpp:67 and timeout cb line 88) only runs on the Finished/timeout branches; if a player disconnects mid-transfer without hitting Finished, the per-player FBufferWriter and timer leak. This is a plausible contributor to #9 (server crash on join): unbounded per-joiner allocation + a raw FMemory::Memcpy slice copy (line 78) with int16 Size truncation of Slices count.
findings.fixDirection: Stream from CurrentBuildingData directly per-slice (serialize slice N on demand) instead of materializing the whole buffer up front; key cleanup on PlayerController logout/destroy, not just Finished/timeout. On the client, deserialize incrementally and free consumed bytes (Buffer.RemoveAt front) so the raw buffer and struct array don't coexist at full size. Validate Slices fits the int16 wire type.

findings.title: TQuadTree<int32> stores a 40-byte FBox2D per building and subdivides densely; BuildingCountMap is small but the tree is not
findings.mechanism: CurrentBuildingQuadTree (h:366) is a TQuadTree<int32> over the full ~750k x 750k cm world. UE's TQuadTree stores each inserted element as {ElementType, FBox2D} = int32(4) + FBox2D(40) ~ 48 B per building (Insert at module .cpp:1198 inserts one box per buildable with a valid VisualBoxCache). That is ~10 MB for 200k and ~48 MB for 1M buildings, on top of CurrentBuildingData and the redirector — plus internal node TArrays that subdivide heavily where factories are dense, adding overhead. The tree's elements are NEVER cheaply removable (the whole redirector workaround exists because TQuadTree<int32> can't update element payloads), so tombstones in the redirector also bloat GetElements results that then get filtered (.cpp:689-708). By contrast BuildingCountMap (h:349, TMap<uint32,uint32>) is bounded by the number of distinct buildable CLASSES (hundreds), so it is negligible — not a leak.
findings.fixDirection: Store culling boxes more compactly (quantized int16 grid cells, ~8 B) or use a uniform spatial grid keyed by stable id so removals are O(1) and no per-element 40 B FBox2D / no redirector is needed. BuildingCountMap can stay as-is.

verdicts.corrections: Severity "critical" is justified given the well-known high-memory complaint, but two nuances: (a) The exact per-building size is layout-dependent — 344 B (scalar FTransform, most likely actual) to 432 B (SIMD-aligned). The analyst's ~360 B is a fair midpoint, not an upper bound; if the build links the ISPC/SIMD math path the cost is ~25% higher (~432 B => 1M buildings ~412 MB). State the figure as a range rather than a precise 360 B. (b) The DataCache variant is sized by its largest alternative (FNormalDataCache, 168-224 B) and is paid for EVERY building including splines/wires that only use the 8-byte FSplineDataCache/FWireData* alternatives — so ~160-216 B is wasted per spline/wire entry on top of the duplication. This makes the variant-driven over-allocation a real, separately-addressable sub-problem (shrinking DataCache, e.g. boxing the rectangle/normal cache behind a pointer, would cut ~150 B/building).
verdicts.extraInsight: Compounding memory leak in the redirector: BuildingDataIndexRedirector (h:365) is, per the in-code comment at h:363, never .Remove()'d when a building is removed — OnBuildingDataAdd at cpp:1198-1206 only ever grows it (Insert into quad tree + linear O(n) reindex loop + .Add), and the quad tree TQuadTree<int32> is likewise append-only. So in a long session of place/remove churn (exactly issue #14's belt-spam repro), CurrentBuildingData entries are removed but the redirector + quad tree keep growing unbounded, adding 4 B/redirector-slot plus quad-tree node overhead that is never reclaimed until a full re-gather. This both (1) leaks memory monotonically and (2) makes the O(n) reindex loop at cpp:1199-1204 progressively slower — a likely contributor to the 15s lag spikes and the ~1h GPU/TDR crash in #14. Worth flagging as its own finding: the second-copy duplication is the static baseline cost, but the redirector/quad-tree append-only growth is the dynamic, unbounded one.

verdicts.corrections: Two minor estimate refinements, neither changing the severity (high stands): (1) "computed in a few FLOPs at draw time" understates the corner recompute: each corner is a full TRS TransformPosition (rotation matrix × vector + translate, ~12-15 flops), so ~50-60 flops for 4 corners plus the 2D affine ScreenPosition map — still cheap (tens of flops/building, dwarfed by the actual Canvas draw cost), but not literally "a few." (2) A naive full recompute at draw time would also re-run the per-class TMap lookups (GetBuildingSize/BuildableSizeOverrideMap, BuildableExtraRotationMap, category-data lookup), which are hash lookups, not flops. The correct fix is therefore not "recompute everything every draw" but "store only what is genuinely non-derivable" — and the per-class data should be looked up once via a per-class cache keyed by BuildableClassHash, not stored per-building. With that, only Size (16B, after the scale multiply) plus the four pointers might be worth keeping per-building; ScreenPosition, Rotation, and Corners (136B) are fully eliminable. Net per-building savings ~136-150B, i.e. ~136-150 MB at 1M buildings, slightly lower than the headline 176 MB but the same order of magnitude.
verdicts.extraInsight: Related amplifier worth flagging: VisualBoxCache (FBox2D ≈ 40B, h:89) is ALSO fully derived from Transform + per-class size (FillInVisualBoxCache recomputes the exact same corners at cpp:526-540 that FillInCache already computed at cpp:423-433 — the work is duplicated and BOTH results are stored). So the total derived/redundant footprint per Normal building is closer to 152B (FNormalDataCache geometry) + 40B (VisualBoxCache) ≈ 192B, not just 176B. Additionally, because FillInCache and FillInVisualBoxCache each independently call GetBuildingSize, build the same 4 corners, and run TransformPosition, every cache fill does the corner transform twice — a redundant CPU cost on the build/redraw hot path (relevant to issue #14's lag spikes), not just a memory cost. Finally, the cache is duplicated across three TArray<FBuildingData> (CurrentBuildingData h:359, PendingAddBuildingData h:370, PendingRemoveBuildingData h:371) plus the client/server transfer copies, so the resident multiplier in transient states is >1×.

verdicts.corrections: Severity high is appropriate but worth qualifying the framing. (a) The 256 MB figure is the conservative floor: a UCanvasRenderTarget2D is a render-targetable resource, so the driver/RHI may also allocate it in a render-target heap and, depending on platform, MSAA=1 here but mip/UAV/clear-optimization metadata can add overhead; 256 MB is the texel storage, real committed VRAM is >=256 MB. (b) The clear-tile cost is bandwidth, not allocation: it is a ~256 MB/pass opaque overwrite of the whole target every build event, which is the per-event GPU thrash, distinct from the one-time 256 MB residency. Both are real; the analyst conflates them slightly but both conclusions hold. (c) Minor wording: allocation is tied to the render resource init of the asset, not literally 'the moment the world loads' — .cpp:394 is the clear, which is the first touch, so practically equivalent.
verdicts.extraInsight: Two cheap algorithmic wins fall straight out of this finding. (1) Replace the full-size FCanvasTileItem ClearItem (.cpp:653-660) with a clear sized to ScissorArea (RedrawArea screen rect) on partial passes — it already computes MinIntX/Y..MaxIntX/Y at .cpp:641-645, so the clear could be {MinIntX,MinIntY}..{MaxIntX,MaxIntY} instead of {0,0}..{8192,8192}, cutting per-event clear bandwidth by orders of magnitude for localized edits (directly addresses issue #14 lag spikes / TDR). (2) The 256 MB residency itself is the dominant fixed VRAM cost and a prime suspect for the 'high memory consumption' complaint and the ~1h GPU TDR in #14; 8192x8192 RGBA8 at PIXEL_PER_CENTIMETER (h:38) gives ~10.9 px/m on a 7.5km x 7.5km world (~1.09 cm/px) — far finer than a factory minimap needs. Dropping to 4096 (RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE = 1024*4) is a one-line/one-asset change that quarters VRAM to 64 MB and quarters every clear+draw bandwidth, and RTF_RGBA8 with a single-channel/alpha-only or RTF_R8 format where color isn't needed would cut another 4x. Also note ORIGIN_UV/PIXEL_PER_CENTIMETER are constexpr off RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE, so resizing the constant is self-consistent in code but must be matched in the uasset (SizeX/SizeY 8192), otherwise transforms desync.

verdicts.corrections:
Mechanism, severity (high), and unbounded-growth direction are all correct. Three refinements to the estimate:

(a) Growth is gated on VisualBoxCache.bIsValid (cpp:1196 and 1215), so only VISIBLE buildables grow the redirector; ignored/invisible ones do not. Belts are visible, so #14 still qualifies. Byte estimate: 4 B/slot is right, but with TArray geometric reallocation the allocated capacity is up to ~1.4-2x the slot count, so steady-state footprint is somewhat above (adds x 4 B).

(b) Tighter Big-O: the scan length equals BuildingDataIndexRedirector.Num(), which BECAUSE of this leak equals cumulative-lifetime-adds, not live building count. So each event is O(cumulative adds), strictly worse than O(live buildings) — the leak makes per-event CPU keep climbing even when live count is flat. This strengthens, not weakens, the quadratic-compound argument.

(c) "Direct contributor to the 15s lag spikes" is slightly overstated as a single-event cause: OnBuildingDataAdd/Remove run INSIDE the frame-time-budgeted RedrawMapCoroutine (co_await Budget per pending item, cpp:557/577), so the scan cost is amortized across frames rather than producing one 15s stall on its own. It is a real contributor to sustained per-frame CPU + memory pressure; the dominant single-event stall is more plausibly the full-clear-and-redraw (#10) plus quad-tree GetElements. Recommend phrasing it as "compounding background cost + leak" rather than "the cause of the 15s freeze."
verdicts.extraInsight: The leak also bloats the quad tree's read path, and there is a latent out-of-bounds hazard. After translating quad-tree ids to redirector values (cpp:691), the resulting array still contains -1 entries from removed buildings; they are NOT explicitly filtered before CurrentBuildingData[i] at cpp:717. The partial-redraw path is saved only by accident: Algo::Sort (cpp:693) puts -1 at the front, and the FindByPredicate(>=Min)/RemoveAt slicing (cpp:696-708) trims everything below Min, and Min is a 0-based CurrentBuildingData index (>=0), so the -1s get sliced off. But (1) this is fragile — any future code path that reads BuildingsToDraw before that slice, or an entire-redraw path that bypassed the redirector, would index CurrentBuildingData[-1]; and (2) GetElements (cpp:686) increasingly returns stale -1-redirected ids as the session runs, so the sort+slice does growing wasted work proportional to the leak. A proper fix (compacting the redirector + reusing freed quad-tree ids via a free-list, or rebuilding the quad tree against live data) would simultaneously cure the memory leak, the O(cumulative-adds) per-event scan, and this wasted read-path work.

findings.title: OnBuildingDataAdd scans the entire BuildingDataIndexRedirector per add → O(N) per add, O(N²) initial load
findings.mechanism: OnBuildingDataAdd (CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp:1194-1210) does a full linear pass over BuildingDataIndexRedirector incrementing every Index>=Pos (cpp:1199-1205) to keep redirector indices in sync with the Z-sorted CurrentBuildingData array. This is O(N) per single add. InitialBuildableGather sorts CurrentBuildingData once, then loops i=0..N-1 calling OnBuildingDataAdd(BuildingData,i) for EVERY building (cpp:522-526). Each call walks a redirector that has already grown to ~i entries → total Σi = O(N²). For a mid/large factory of N≈50,000 lightweight+heavy buildables that is ~1.25e9 inner iterations of branchy integer work on the game thread; at N≈200,000 (megabase) it is ~2e10. This is the dominant cost of the multi-second load hang and the ~15s 'recovery' after the build burst settles — every queued add eventually re-runs this O(N) scan once the redraw coroutine restarts. Note the redirector scan is NOT inside the co_await Budget loop of RedrawMapCoroutine (the await is per added building, cpp:577, but the O(N) redirector walk happens synchronously inside OnBuildingDataAdd), so a single heavy add cannot be time-sliced and will blow the frame budget on its own once N is large.
findings.fixDirection: Eliminate the parallel index-shift entirely: have the quadtree store a stable building handle/ID (monotonic, never reused) instead of a positional index into CurrentBuildingData, and resolve handle→data via a TMap<Handle,FBuildingData*> or a free-list slab so inserts/removes are O(log N) (tree) + O(1) (map). For the initial bulk load, build the quadtree once from the already-sorted array without per-element redirector rewrites (bulk insert), turning O(N²) into O(N log N).

findings.title: OnBuildingDataRemove + linear find in RedrawMapCoroutine → O(N) per remove, O(K·N) mass dismantle
findings.mechanism: Two stacked linear scans per removed building. (1) RedrawMapCoroutine locates the victim with Algo::LowerBound on Z (cpp:584) then linearly scans forward comparing full FBuildingData==FBuildingData (cpp:587-605); because the array is sorted ONLY by Z (operator<=> compares Transform.Z only, CartographDataStructure.cpp:23-26), all co-planar buildings (a flat foundation field / a belt floor all share one Z) collapse into a single LowerBound bucket, so this inner scan is O(N) in the worst (and very common) case, with an FTransform.Equals + variant compare each step. (2) OnBuildingDataRemove (cpp:1213-1234) then walks the ENTIRE redirector to find the matching slot, set it to -1, and decrement every index>Pos → O(N). Net O(N) per remove → O(K·N) to dismantle K. Mass-dismantling a large structure (K in the thousands) on an N≈50k base is ~K·50k ≈ 1e8–1e9 ops, all on the game thread, matching the reported multi-second freezes on dismantle. RemoveAt(i) on CurrentBuildingData (cpp:597) additionally shifts the tail → another O(N).
findings.fixDirection: Index buildings by a spatial-hash or by the engine's own buildable handle so removal is O(log N)/O(1) instead of scanning. Replace the Z-only ordering+linear match with a hash map keyed on a stable identity (class hash + quantized transform, or the FG instance index). Avoid CurrentBuildingData.RemoveAt mid-array shifts by using a slotted/free-list container or tombstones compacted lazily.

findings.title: Every build/remove event cancels the in-flight redraw coroutine and restarts from scratch — the map never converges mid-drag
findings.mechanism: All five build/remove hooks call RedrawMap(false) unconditionally (cpp:142,173,202,234,264) and the multicast client path does too (CartographModSubsystem.cpp:46). RedrawMap (cpp:435-451): if a redraw coroutine is already running (not initializing) it Cancel()s it (cpp:442) and sets IsPendingRedraw; OnCoroutineFinishedOrCancelled (cpp:895-913) then immediately restarts via ExecuteRedrawMapCoroutine. The pending Add/Remove arrays are only drained when the coroutine actually executes (ExecuteRedrawMapCoroutine empties them, cpp:930-931). When dragging a belt/foundation row or stamping a blueprint, hooks fire many times per frame; each fire cancels the partially-completed draw before it can finish, so the canvas-clear + redraw work done so far is thrown away and re-issued. With a build rate faster than one full redraw, the coroutine is in a permanent cancel→restart loop and produces ZERO completed frames until the player stops building — at which point one final O(N·draws) redraw runs. This is the structural cause of the 'lag spikes up to 15s' in #14: cost is not just per-building, it is (events during drag) × (cost of the bookkeeping that survives cancellation, which includes the FCancellationGuard-protected O(N) add/remove processing in cpp:561-617 that runs to completion every restart). The FCancellationGuard (cpp:562) means the entire add/remove ingestion block is non-cancellable, so each restart re-pays it.
findings.fixDirection: Decouple ingestion from drawing. Drain PendingAdd/Remove into the data structures continuously (cheap incremental ops, see other findings), but coalesce DRAW requests: accumulate a dirty-rect and (re)start at most one draw per frame after a short debounce/quiescence, rather than cancel-restart on every event. Never throw away completed draw work; expand the dirty region instead. This directly implements #10's 'localized redraws + frame-relative budget + explicit full redraw' ask.

findings.title: Every redraw clears and redraws into an 8192×8192 (256 MB) render target; partial redraws still issue a full-screen clear tile
findings.mechanism: RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE = 1024*8 = 8192 (header:35); the canvas render target is 8192×8192. At RGBA8 that is 8192·8192·4 = 268,435,456 bytes ≈ 256 MB of VRAM resident permanently (more if the canvas target is float/HDR). Every RedrawMapCoroutine pass draws a full-size ClearItem tile of {RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE,RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE} (cpp:653-660) covering the whole 8192² surface, then relies on a scissor rect (CartographCanvasRenderItem.cpp:104-106, ScissorArea) to clip it to the dirty region. The scissor limits the pixels actually written, but the per-redraw cost still includes issuing the full clear primitive and, on entire redraws (IsRedrawingEntirely, set by every OnZFilterUpdated→RedrawMap(true) and on init), rasterizing all visible buildings across the full 256 MB target. Combined with the cancel/restart thrash, the GPU is asked to clear+repaint a 256 MB target repeatedly per second during a drag — a direct candidate for the GPU driver TDR/timeout crash after sustained building reported in #14. The render target is allocated regardless of how small the player's factory is.
findings.fixDirection: Tile the render target (e.g. 8×8 grid of 1024² tiles) and only clear/redraw dirty tiles, or drop to 4096² and scale icons. Replace the full-surface ClearItem with a clear restricted to the dirty rect (RHIClear with scissor, or draw the clear tile sized to ScissorArea, not the whole texture). Allocate the target lazily / size it to the populated map extent so empty saves don't pay 256 MB.

findings.title: BuildingDataIndexRedirector and the quadtree grow without bound; removed entries are never reclaimed (tombstones leak)
findings.mechanism: By design (header:361-366) the redirector array is never .Remove()'d: on removal OnBuildingDataRemove sets the slot to -1 (cpp:1224) but leaves it in BuildingDataIndexRedirector forever, and CurrentBuildingQuadTree.Insert appends a new redirector slot for every add (cpp:1198, keyed on BuildingDataIndexRedirector.Num()). Over a long play session with normal churn (build/dismantle/rebuild, belt re-routing, blueprint re-stamping) the redirector and the quadtree leaf element lists grow monotonically with the TOTAL number of buildings ever created, not the number currently present. This makes every O(N) redirector scan in OnBuildingDataAdd/Remove get strictly slower over time (N = lifetime placements, not live count), and the quadtree GetElements (cpp:686) returns an ever-growing pile of stale -1 entries that must be mapped (cpp:689-692) and sorted (cpp:693) before being filtered out by the Min/Max predicate (cpp:696-697). This is both a steadily worsening CPU cost AND a genuine memory leak that grows for the entire session — a strong contributor to the 'high memory consumption' complaint and to the ~1h-to-crash timeline in #14 (cost per build event keeps rising until a redraw blows the frame/GPU budget).
findings.fixDirection: Switch the quadtree to store stable IDs with real removal (UE TQuadTree supports Remove with the original box; reuse freed IDs via a free-list) so the structure tracks LIVE count, not lifetime count. Eliminate the redirector entirely (see redirector-on-add finding). Periodically (or on full redraw) rebuild the tree from the live array to compact tombstones if incremental removal is impractical.

findings.title: Initial load copies the entire engine lightweight-buildable map by value (second full copy of the factory in RAM)
findings.mechanism: OnWorldLoaded launches InitialBuildableGather passing AFGLightweightBuildableSubsystem::Get(World)->mBuildableClassToInstanceArray (cpp:387). InitialBuildableGather's signature takes Buildings BY VALUE (CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp:455-456, declared header:201; the comment cpp:454 even says 'Intentional copies'). mBuildableClassToInstanceArray is TMap<TSubclassOf<AFGBuildable>, TArray<FRuntimeBuildableInstanceData>> (FGLightweightBuildableSubsystem.h:839) and holds the BULK of a modern Satisfactory factory — every belt/pipe/foundation/wire migrated to the lightweight system, each entry a full FRuntimeBuildableInstanceData (FTransform[~48-96B] + customization + type-specific dynamic struct). Copying it by value transiently doubles that entire dataset in RAM at load (potentially hundreds of MB for a large base) and is itself an O(N) deep copy of every transform. Simultaneously CurrentBuildingData is built as a THIRD parallel copy (each FBuildingData also stores Transform + extra data + caches, cpp:491,513). The coroutine then holds the copied map alive for the whole gather. The Factories array is likewise copied by value (cpp:455, also '// Intentional copies'). This is a primary driver of the load-time memory spike and the general high-memory complaint.
findings.fixDirection: Pass the engine map by const-reference (or iterate it in place) instead of copying — the gather only reads it. Build CurrentBuildingData incrementally and reserve once (it already Empty(Total)s, cpp:467) but avoid materializing FBuildingData fields that can be recomputed lazily at draw time. Consider storing only a compact record (class hash + quantized transform + box) and deriving draw caches on demand to shrink the per-building footprint of the third copy.

findings.title: co_await Budget is issued per draw-primitive (every spline segment, every rectangle edge), inflating suspend/resume and bookkeeping overhead vs. issue #10's frame-budget request
findings.mechanism: The budget IS frame-relative already (FTickTimeBudget: await_ready returns true and does NOT suspend until CyclesPerTick of wall-time have elapsed this tick, then resumes next GFrameCounter — TickTimeBudget.cpp:76-96), which is the correct model #10 asks for. The problem is GRANULARITY and per-primitive accounting cost: RedrawMapCoroutine awaits Budget after the tile of every rectangle (cpp:801) AND after EACH of its 4 outline edges (cpp:806,808,810,811), and after EACH of the up-to-SPLINE_SEGMENTS(8) line segments of every spline (cpp:830), plus once per building (cpp:884). For a base of B drawn buildings dominated by belts/pipes (splines), that is ~9·B co_await evaluations per full redraw; each await_ready reads FPlatformTime::Cycles() and the coroutine machinery checks suspension. Even when not suspending this is millions of awaiter calls + a Cycles() syscall-ish read per primitive on a 50k-building redraw, measurable game-thread overhead on top of the actual draw. It also makes the budget coarse in the wrong direction: because suspension can only happen AT an await point, a building with heavy synchronous pre-work (the O(N) redirector ops, or AsyncLoadObject of an unloaded icon mid-loop, cpp:758) can still overrun the per-tick budget badly.
findings.fixDirection: Keep the FTickTimeBudget model but await ONCE per building (or per small batch of K buildings), not per primitive — draw a whole rectangle/spline as a unit between yields. Pre-resolve all icon textures before the draw loop so AsyncLoadObject never stalls mid-redraw. Expose the dirty-rect 'localized redraw' and an explicit user-triggered full-redraw button per #10 instead of implicitly full-redrawing on every Z-filter change (OnZFilterUpdated→RedrawMap(true), cpp:948).

findings.title: Dedicated server runs full O(N²) ingestion and per-event multicast even though it never draws, amplifying join-time crash risk
findings.mechanism: On a dedicated server RedrawMapCoroutine still executes the entire add/remove ingestion block (the O(N) LowerBound/Insert/OnBuildingDataAdd/Remove work, cpp:561-617) and only co_returns BEFORE the canvas work at cpp:619-621 (FPlatformProperties::IsServerOnly). So the server pays the full O(N²) initial gather and O(N) per-event bookkeeping with zero rendering benefit. Worse, every build/remove on the server triggers ExecuteRedrawMapCoroutine which calls ACartographModSubsystem::Instance->ClientUpdateBuildingData (NetMulticast Reliable) with the pending add/remove arrays (cpp:919-928), and the join handshake serializes the ENTIRE CurrentBuildingData into a FBufferWriter at once (CartographRemoteCallObject.cpp:48-53) then slices it. A player joining mid-session triggers ServerRequestInitialBuildingData which Archive << CurrentBuildingData (one giant serialization of all N buildings on the game thread) while the server is simultaneously running the O(N²) gather/cancel-restart loop for any concurrent building — a plausible mechanism for the intermittent join crash in #9 (reliable multicast buffer overflow / serialization of a huge array under memory pressure during the O(N²) spike).
findings.fixDirection: On a dedicated server skip the draw-oriented bookkeeping entirely (the quadtree/redirector are only needed for localized DRAW); keep only the authoritative CurrentBuildingData list needed for replication. Batch/coalesce ClientUpdateBuildingData instead of one multicast per build event, and chunk/stream the initial CurrentBuildingData serialization off the critical path (or build it incrementally) so a join doesn't allocate+serialize the whole array in one game-thread call during a build spike.

verdicts.corrections:
One precision correction (does not lower severity): the complexity is O(M²) in M = buildables with VisualBoxCache.bIsValid (i.e. actually-DRAWN buildables), not raw N. FillInCache (CartographDataStructure.cpp:264-446) leaves VisualBoxCache invalid for zero-size buildings, missing category/layer/spline/wire data, or Thickness<=0 (early returns at 304/340/363/374/520), and OnBuildingDataAdd skips those entirely (guard at cpp:1196). In a real factory M≈N (foundations, machines, belts, pipes, walls all draw), so the analyst's 50k/200k estimates hold within a small constant factor — severity stays critical. Also note the InitialBuildableGather O(M²) pass (cpp:522-526) is fully synchronous (no co_await), so it cannot even be time-sliced — this is a stronger statement than "blows the frame budget": it is a single uninterruptible multi-second-to-minute game-thread stall, matching the load hang in issues #1/#3.</corrections>
<parameter name="extraInsight">During InitialBuildableGather the entire O(M²) redirector work is PROVABLY WASTED. The array is pre-sorted (cpp:520) and processed in increasing order with Pos=i. At step i the redirector only contains values that are a subset of {0..i-1}, all strictly less than Pos=i, so the branch `if (Index >= Pos)` at cpp:1201 is NEVER true and zero increments ever happen — yet it still scans M(M-1)/2 entries. The redirector for the initial load could be built in a single O(M) pass (it is just the identity/compacted mapping over valid entries), eliminating the entire O(M²) term for free without changing behavior. This is the single highest-leverage algorithmic fix for the load hang.

Second related problem: the increment-every-index design makes BOTH OnBuildingDataAdd (O(M) scan, cpp:1199) and OnBuildingDataRemove (O(M) scan, cpp:1217-1230) linear because the redirector stores absolute CurrentBuildingData indices that must be shifted on every insert/remove into the Z-sorted array. The proper fix is to make CurrentBuildingData insertion/removal not renumber everything (e.g. stable IDs / a free-list / generation handles, or storing the QuadTree payload as a stable handle instead of an array index), which would drop per-add and per-remove from O(M) to O(log M) and the initial load / join from O(M²) to O(M log M). Note CurrentBuildingData.Insert at cpp:575 is itself an O(M) memmove per live add (sorted insert into a TArray), so even after fixing the redirector, the array-shift remains a secondary O(M) per-add term to address for full megabase scaling.</extraInsight>
</invoke>

Two refinements, both making the picture worse, not better. (a) The inner remove scan at cpp:587-605 is bounded by M = number of buildings sharing the victim's exact Z (it breaks at :600 when Z is exceeded), not literally N; on flat fields M≈large-fraction-of-N so the conclusion stands, but state it as O(M). (b) The truly dominant and unconditional cost is the redirector walk in OnBuildingDataRemove/OnBuildingDataAdd, which is O(redirector size), and the redirector is NEVER compacted: header comment at CartographGameInstanceModule.h:363 says it 'doesn't get .Remove()'d when a building is removed' — line 1224 only tombstones the slot to -1, and the only resets are .Empty() on full re-init (cpp:290, cpp:468). So redirector size = cumulative count of all buildings ever added since the last full redraw, which is ≥ N and grows monotonically across the session. The per-event cost is therefore O(total-ever-built), strictly worse than O(N) on a base with churn. Severity 'critical' is correct.
verdicts.extraInsight: The never-compacted redirector + quad-tree is also a standalone MEMORY leak (the well-known 'high memory' complaint): every dismantle leaves a dead int32 in BuildingDataIndexRedirector and a dead entry in CurrentBuildingQuadTree (TQuadTree<int32>, declared CartographGameInstanceModule.h:365-366; CurrentBuildingQuadTree.Remove at cpp:1223 removes the value but the redirector slot and accumulated tree node churn persist), so a session that builds and dismantles heavily grows both structures without bound until a full redraw rebuilds them. This both leaks memory and progressively slows every subsequent add/remove (O(redirector) keeps rising) — a compounding feedback that matches issue #14's 'gets worse over ~1h then TDR/crash' description better than a fixed O(K·N) alone. Fix direction: replace the redirector with a free-list/generational handle (O(1) tombstone reuse) or store the CurrentBuildingData index directly in the quad-tree payload and update it on RemoveAt, and replace LowerBound-by-Z + full-struct== with a stable unique key (e.g. hash of class+quantized transform) in a TMap for O(1) locate; also avoid RemoveAt tail-shift by swapping to a stable-id store. That collapses per-event cost from O(N)/O(total-built) to ~O(log N) or O(1) and removes the leak.

verdicts.corrections: No correction to severity (critical is appropriate) or to the mechanism. The cost estimate should be tightened upward: the per-restart non-cancellable ingestion is Theta(N) per queued element, not merely the LowerBound. Two stacked O(N) sources: (a) CurrentBuildingData.Insert/RemoveAt memmoves (cpp:575, 597), and (b) the full-array reindex loops inside OnBuildingDataAdd (cpp:1199-1205) and OnBuildingDataRemove (cpp:1218-1230). The Algo::LowerBound is only O(log N) and is the cheap part. The dominant per-event uncancellable cost is the linear array/redirector work.
verdicts.extraInsight: Related amplifiers found while verifying: (1) RedrawArea accumulates the VisualBoxCache of every ingested add/remove across restarts without being reset between cancellations (cpp:570, 593); RedrawArea is only cleared at successful completion (cpp:888-889) or the early-out co_returns. Because partial redraws almost never reach completion during a drag, the localized-redraw scissor region (cpp:639-651) monotonically grows to encompass the whole drag, defeating the localized-redraw optimization that #10 asked for — the final redraw effectively covers a large bounding box. (2) OnBuildingDataRemove uses BuildingCountMap.FindChecked (cpp:1233), which will crash (check failure) if a remove arrives for a class hash not present — relevant to the dedicated-server join/crash reports (#9) where client/server PendingRemove ordering can desync. (3) The redirector reindex loops mean even the "localized" path has an irreducible O(N) per building added/removed regardless of redraw budget, so a frame-relative redraw budget alone (as suggested in #10) would not fix the ingestion cost — the fix needs a different index structure (e.g., stable IDs / generation-indexed slots) so add/remove is O(log N) rather than O(N).

verdicts.corrections: One precision correction to the mechanism wording, not the severity: for ordinary BUILD/REMOVE events the path is RedrawMap(false) (cpp:142,173,202,234,264), i.e. IsRedrawingEntirely is false, so the scissor (cpp:641-645) does clip the clear+raster to the dirty AABB. So during a placement drag the GPU is NOT literally repainting all 256 MB per event for builds — the full-size ClearItem primitive is still *submitted* (cpp:653-660, correctly stated by the analyst), but the actual pixel writes are scissor-limited to the changed region. The literal "clear+repaint a 256 MB target" applies to (a) every OnZFilterUpdated→RedrawMap(true), (b) init, and (c) any code path with IsRedrawingEntirely set. The analyst already scoped this correctly to "on entire redraws (IsRedrawingEntirely)", so the finding is accurate; only the closing sentence "clear+repaint a 256 MB target repeatedly per second during a drag" slightly overstates the build-event case (cost there is full-clear-submission + cancel/restart overhead + clipped raster, not a full 256 MB repaint). Severity stays high.
verdicts.extraInsight: Two adjacent problems found while verifying: (1) The cancel/restart design (cpp:442 + cpp:912) makes the "redraw budget" largely ineffective during rapid activity: a redraw is canceled mid-flight and restarted from scratch (re-issuing the full ClearItem and re-running the QuadTree query/sort at cpp:686-708), so under a fast belt-drag the coroutine may never reach completion, wasting the already-spent clear/setup cost every frame — this is a stronger explanation for the 15s lag spikes in #14 than the raw target size alone. (2) BuildingDataIndexRedirector is documented at h:362-365 as never being .Remove()'d when buildings are removed ("The redirector array doesn't get .Remove()'d") and the QuadTree elements are never updated, so the quad-tree/redirector grow monotonically with total lifetime build+remove operations, not with current building count — an unbounded memory/lookup-cost growth that compounds the high-memory complaint and slows the partial-redraw GetElements path (cpp:686) over a long session, consistent with the ~1h-to-crash timeline in #14.

verdicts.corrections:
Severity should be downgraded from high to low/medium. Two estimate errors: (1) The quadtree/GetElements pollution is the wrong mechanism — Remove() genuinely removes from the tree, so GetElements returns only live elements and is NOT polluted by -1 tombstones; the sort/filter at cpp:693/696-697 are bounded by live count, not lifetime. (2) Memory magnitude is overstated: the leak is one int32 (4 bytes) per lifetime placement, ~4 MB per million placements — a real but minor leak, not "a strong contributor to high memory consumption." The dominant memory costs are elsewhere (the 8192x8192 RGBA8 render target alone is ~256 MB, plus the FBuildingData caches in CurrentBuildingData). (3) Crash/#14 attribution is weak: the per-event redirector scans (cpp:1199-1205, 1218-1230) do grow O(lifetime) and add steadily rising CPU per build event, which is a legitimate scaling concern, but the claimed path to the GPU TDR (redraw/draw budget blown by stale entries) does not hold because the draw set and quadtree query are live-count bounded. The leak is a slow CPU-scaling and minor memory issue, not a credible driver of the 1h GPU timeout.</corrections>
<extraInsight>The redirector design is the actual algorithmic smell, independent of the leak: it converts what should be O(log N) spatial bookkeeping into O(N) full-array scans on EVERY single add/remove (cpp:1199-1205 reindex-all on add; cpp:1218-1230 scan-all on remove). Combined with the callers in RedrawMapCoroutine — Algo::LowerBound + CurrentBuildingData.Insert at cpp:573-575 and the linear search + RemoveAt at cpp:584-597, both O(live N) due to array shifting — processing a batch of K build events is O(K*N). A stable element id (e.g. store the CurrentBuildingData index indirection via a free-list or a TMap<id,index>, or store the building's stable GUID in the tree) would remove both the O(N) reindex and the leak. Separately, UE's TQuadTree never collapses emptied split subnodes after Remove, so the tree's NODE structure (not element lists) retains peak spatial subdivision for the session — a bounded, secondary retention worth noting but far smaller than the claimed effect.</extraInsight>
</invoke>

findings.title: co_await Budget bounds only game-thread CPU; the entire redraw is ONE unbounded GPU draw pass -> TDR crash
findings.mechanism: RedrawMapCoroutine accumulates every Canvas->DrawItem into a single FCanvas instance opened by BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget (cpp:630) and only flushed by EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget in OnCoroutineFinishedOrCancelled (cpp:901). The co_await Budget yields (cpp:577,607,687,801,830,884) ONLY pace the game thread that *emits* batched elements; they never flush to the GPU. All accumulated batches are submitted to the render thread at once and drawn in a single RHI pass inside FCartographCanvasRenderItem::Render_GameThread's AddPass lambda (CanvasRenderItem.cpp:108-114), which calls BatchedElements.Draw() once per batch with no yielding. For a full redraw (bRedrawEntirely) of a large factory, BuildingsToDraw spans Min..Max over all CurrentBuildingData (cpp:676-682); each rectangle emits 1 tile + 4 line DrawItems (cpp:800-811), each spline emits 8 lines (SPLINE_SEGMENTS, cpp:825-831), so 100k buildings => roughly 0.5-1M batched primitives = millions of triangles rasterized into an 8192x8192 target in ONE GPU submission. On a single VSYNC/present interval that exceeds the Windows TDR threshold (~2s of no GPU progress) and the driver resets the device, crashing the client. This is the exact mechanism behind issue #14's 'GPU driver timeout after placing a belt': a belt is a spline/conveyor whose VisualBoxCache or a Z-filter/layer toggle promotes the redraw to a full redraw, re-emitting the whole factory in one pass. The RedrawTimeBudget config is therefore a false sense of safety: it can make a redraw take many game-thread frames yet still produce one giant GPU pass.
findings.fixDirection: Decouple GPU cost from element count: composite the map from persistent per-tile sub-targets (e.g. 256x256 grid of 512px tiles over the 8192 space) and only re-render dirty tiles per frame; cap GPU work per frame by flushing/EndDraw after a bounded number of primitives or a bounded scissor area and resuming next tick (multi-frame incremental compositing) so no single RHI submission rasterizes the whole factory. Persist the target across redraws instead of full clear+redraw.

findings.title: Full-screen 8192x8192 opaque ClearItem emitted on EVERY redraw, including tiny incremental ones
findings.mechanism: Every RedrawMapCoroutine pass builds an FCanvasTileItem covering {0,0}..{RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE,RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE} with SE_BLEND_Opaque and calls Canvas->DrawItem(ClearItem) (cpp:653-660). On a partial redraw the ScissorArea clips this to RedrawArea (CanvasRenderItem.cpp:104-106), so it is functionally correct, BUT: (1) on a full redraw it is a full 8192^2 = 67.1M-texel opaque overwrite (~256 MB write traffic at RGBA8) submitted in the same single pass as the geometry, adding fixed fill cost on top of finding gpu-one-pass; (2) the clear and the building draws share ScissorArea, set once per batch from Instance->ScissorArea — but ScissorArea is mutated on the GAME thread (cpp:635/645) while batches are consumed on the RENDER thread, and a single coroutine pass uses exactly one ScissorArea value, so clear+draw are consistently clipped within one redraw. The real waste is that a localized single-belt add still re-clears its whole RedrawArea rectangle (expanded by BoxExpansionCentimeters=300 each side, cpp:545) and redraws every neighbor overlapping that box (quad-tree GetElements, cpp:686), so even 'incremental' redraws scale with local building density, not with 1.
findings.fixDirection: Replace the draw-a-full-opaque-tile clear with a true scissored RHIClear (RHICmdList.ClearRenderTargetView under the scissor) or a persistent target that is never fully cleared; for incremental updates clear only the exact dirty tiles. Shrink BoxExpansionCentimeters or apply it only to line/spline types that actually need anti-alias bleed margin, to reduce neighbor over-draw.

findings.title: 8192x8192 RGBA8 render target = 256 MB VRAM, plus auto-mip chain regenerated every redraw
findings.mechanism: RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE = 1024*8 = 8192 (header:35) and the asset CanvasRenderTarget_BuildingVisualization is RTF_RGBA8 (confirmed in uasset). Base mip = 8192*8192*4 bytes = 268.4 MB of VRAM for a single 2D map texture that is mostly empty for most factories. The asset also carries bAutoGenerateMips (confirmed in uasset), which adds ~33% (~89 MB) for the mip chain AND, critically, makes EndDrawCanvasToRenderTarget (cpp:901) kick off a full-resolution mip-generation pass over the entire 8192^2 texture on EVERY redraw — even a one-belt incremental redraw that the scissor otherwise limited to a few hundred pixels. So auto-mips silently defeat the scissor optimization: each redraw pays a whole-texture GPU pass regardless of dirty area. Total ~357 MB VRAM resident is a large fraction of the well-known high-memory complaint, and the per-redraw mip pass is a second uncapped GPU cost feeding the TDR in #14.
findings.fixDirection: Disable bAutoGenerateMips on the render target (or generate mips lazily only when the map UI is open and only for dirty tiles). Reconsider 8192 RGBA8: a tiled/virtual-texture scheme or a smaller base with on-demand higher-detail tiles would cut the 256 MB floor dramatically; if mips are needed for zoom, build them from a tile cache rather than one monolithic 67M-texel surface.

findings.title: FCanvas::GetBatchedElements hook globally replaces EVERY canvas batch in the game with FCartographCanvasRenderItem
findings.mechanism: SUBSCRIBE_METHOD(FCanvas::GetBatchedElements, ...) (cpp:322-354) overrides batched-element allocation for ALL FCanvas usage process-wide, not just the map's render-to-target canvas. Every HUD element, every UMG/Slate batched-element draw, debug lines, etc. now allocates a heap FCartographCanvasRenderItem via 'new' (cpp:349) and routes through the custom Render_GameThread/Render_RenderThread (CanvasRenderItem.cpp). Per-frame this adds: an extra branch evaluating IsCartograph = Instance && Canvas == Instance->CurrentCanvas for every batch (CanvasRenderItem.cpp:91), a heap allocation per new batch, and a virtual dispatch through the replacement class for unrelated UI. The IsMatch/Last()-reuse logic (cpp:339-351) mirrors stock UE behavior so correctness is plausible, but any divergence from the engine's real FCanvasBatchedElementRenderItem (e.g. the two Render paths each manage Data deletion differently: Render_RenderThread DeferredDelete vs Render_GameThread raw delete, CanvasRenderItem.cpp:42-43 vs 119) risks leaks/double-free on canvases the mod never intended to touch. This is a system-wide tax to apply a scissor that is only ever needed for one specific canvas.
findings.fixDirection: Stop hooking GetBatchedElements globally. Either (a) early-out the override when Canvas != the map's CurrentCanvas so all other canvases keep the stock fast path with zero new allocation, or (b) drop the canvas hook entirely and apply the scissor via a dedicated render target draw pass / RDG scissor set around the map's own EndDraw, so unrelated game UI is never rerouted through mod code.

findings.title: Async texture load inside the draw loop can stall/extend the open canvas pass; icons re-fetched every redraw
findings.mechanism: Inside the per-building draw loop, for Icon buildings the code does Texture->Get() and, if not resident, co_await UE5Coro::Latent::AsyncLoadObject(*Texture) (cpp:755-758) WHILE the FCanvas opened at cpp:630 is still mid-accumulation. The comment at cpp:754 says the texture may be unloaded between redraws so it cannot be cached, meaning on a full redraw with many distinct icon types, the coroutine repeatedly suspends mid-pass for streaming I/O, holding the BeginDraw/EndDraw scope open across many frames (RenderContext lives the whole time). This lengthens the window in which CurrentCanvas/ScissorArea are mutable and delays the single GPU flush further; if a redraw is cancelled (RedrawMap Cancel, cpp:442) mid-load the partially-built canvas is still flushed by OnCoroutineFinishedOrCancelled, producing a partial map. It also means icon UTexture2D resources are pulled in on demand each redraw rather than kept resident, adding streaming churn that compounds the redraw cost.
findings.fixDirection: Pre-resolve and pin all icon textures (keep hard refs / AddToRoot or a streaming-priority hold) before opening the canvas, so the draw loop never suspends on I/O between BeginDraw and EndDraw; batch icon draws by texture to minimize batch breaks. Pin only while the map feature is active.

findings.title: co_await Budget between every line/outline causes excessive batch fragmentation and yields, not GPU bounding
findings.mechanism: The draw loop co_awaits the time budget after almost every primitive: per rectangle it yields after the tile and after each of the 4 outline lines (cpp:801,806,808,810,812), per spline after each of 8 segment lines (cpp:830), and once more per building (cpp:884). For N buildings this is on the order of 5N-9N coroutine suspensions per full redraw. Each suspension is a game-thread tick boundary, so a full redraw of a large factory is spread over thousands of frames of micro-work, which (combined with finding gpu-one-pass) means the map can stay 'redrawing' for a very long wall-clock time while still ultimately emitting one big GPU pass. Frequent suspension also interleaves new build events that call RedrawMap and Cancel the in-flight coroutine (cpp:441-445), so under active building the redraw may never converge, continually re-emitting work — a plausible contributor to the sustained lag spikes in #14 (#14 notes 15s spikes when placing/removing).
findings.fixDirection: Budget by accumulated primitive/area cost, not per-line; emit whole buildings between yields, and coalesce rapid build events (debounce the dirty-rect set) so one redraw covers many events instead of cancel/restart per event. Tie yields to a real GPU-cost estimate so the budget meaningfully bounds the eventual pass.

verdicts.corrections:
Two precision fixes, neither changes the verdict or critical severity. (1) "single RHI pass" / "one RHI pass" is an oversimplification: the flush produces N AddPass lambdas, one per batch grouped by texture/blendmode/elementtype/transform (CanvasRenderItem.cpp:89, IsMatch at CanvasRenderItem.h:76-84), not literally one pass. But they all execute in a single flush within one render frame with zero GPU-side yielding, so the operative claim ("submitted at once, no yielding, one present interval") is correct. (2) The spline citation is slightly loose: the literal loop bound at cpp:825-826 is Points.Num()-1, not SPLINE_SEGMENTS directly; SPLINE_SEGMENTS=8 is applied at point-generation time (CartographDataStructure.cpp:225-227), yielding 9 points => 8 lines. The "8 lines per spline" figure is correct.</corrections>
<parameter name="extraInsight">The #14 belt-trigger is better explained by redraw promotion than by the belt's own spline geometry. A single belt placed via the localized path calls RedrawMap(false) (cpp:142/173/202/234/264) and is scissor-clipped to its VisualBoxCache (cpp:568,591,639-645). What converts a belt placement into a full-factory re-emit is: (a) IsRedrawingEntirely |= bRedrawEntirely being sticky (cpp:559) so any concurrently-queued full redraw (init at cpp:541, or a Z-filter layer toggle via OnZFilterUpdated->RedrawMap(true) at cpp:948) coalesces ALL pending adds into one entire redraw; and (b) the new building's VisualBoxCache.bIsValid gating (cpp:568) — if invalid, RedrawArea is never expanded, but IsRedrawingEntirely stays whatever it was. So the right fix target is not just the GPU pass but also (1) splitting the single flush into multiple BeginDraw/EndDraw cycles with a per-frame primitive/draw-call budget so the GPU work itself is chunked, and (2) keeping full redraws spatially tiled (render the 8192x8192 target in K scissor tiles across K frames) instead of one full-target clear+draw. Separately, the full-redraw path does NOT use CurrentBuildingQuadTree at all (cpp:676-682 vs the localized path at cpp:686), so even a tile-based full redraw could cull per-tile via the quad tree to cut overdraw.

Two nuance corrections, neither lowers severity. (a) The claim says clear and draws are "submitted in the same single pass as the geometry" and share "exactly one ScissorArea value" per redraw — true in practice, but the precise mechanism is that every DrawItem (the clear plus each TileItem/line) appends to the canvas BatchedElements list, which is flushed by the single custom FCartographCanvasRenderItem render pass that reads Instance->ScissorArea once at flush time (CanvasRenderItem.cpp:104). It's one scissor value per *flush*, and a flush can be triggered mid-coroutine, but within one RedrawMapCoroutine invocation ScissorArea is written exactly once (cpp:635 or 645) before any DrawItem, so the analyst's conclusion (clear+draw consistently clipped together) holds. (b) The thread-safety remark is accurate but should be downgraded from a concern to benign: ScissorArea is a plain std::array<uint32,4> (header:375) written on the game thread (cpp:635/645) and read on the render thread (CanvasRenderItem.cpp:104) with no fence/atomic — but BeginDrawCanvasToRenderTarget + co_await NextTick ordering and the once-per-pass write make a torn read effectively impossible here, so it is not an additional bug, just a latent fragility.
verdicts.extraInsight: The opaque full-screen clear is strictly wasteful even on full redraws: it clears to {0,0,0,0} with SE_BLEND_Opaque, which is exactly what a hardware fast-clear / RTV clear does for free at no fill cost. Routing this through Canvas->DrawItem turns a free clear into a 67M-texel rasterized opaque quad pushed through the batched-elements pixel pipeline every single redraw. Replacing it with UKismetRenderingLibrary::ClearRenderTarget2D (or a scissored RHIClear) would eliminate the 268MB/full-redraw fill entirely and, for partial redraws, a scissored clear is far cheaper than a full-quad-clipped-by-scissor tile. Separately, the BoxExpansionCentimeters=300 padding compounds the cost quadratically for clustered builds: dense belt/wire runs (issue #14's trigger is "placing a belt") produce many overlapping 300cm-padded boxes whose union RedrawArea can balloon to cover a large local region, so GetElements (cpp:686) returns and redraws a large neighbor set per belt segment — turning a 1-belt edit into an O(N_local) redraw, which matches the reported 15s spikes far better than the fixed clear cost alone.

verdicts.corrections: Severity should be downgraded from high to medium. The genuinely-supported cost is a single resident ~256 MiB (268.4 MB) RGBA8 render target — real and worth fixing, but it is one fixed allocation, not a per-frame runaway. Estimate corrections: total VRAM is ~256 MiB, NOT ~357 MB; remove the +89 MB / +33% mip-chain figure entirely (bAutoGenerateMips = False). There is no per-redraw mip-generation pass, so this finding does NOT contribute the claimed 'second uncapped GPU cost' to the #14 TDR.
verdicts.extraInsight: The actual per-redraw whole-texture risk is elsewhere and is real: RedrawMapCoroutine unconditionally draws a full-size opaque clear quad every redraw — FCanvasTileItem ClearItem with size {RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE, RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE} (8192x8192), BlendMode SE_BLEND_Opaque, Canvas->DrawItem(ClearItem) at Private/CartographGameInstanceModule.cpp:653-660. For an incremental (non-entire) redraw this is what the scissor (ScissorArea set at cpp:635/645 and applied via the custom CartographCanvasRenderItem) clips down to the dirty rect, so the scissor is what keeps incremental redraws cheap. Two practical levers for the memory complaint: (1) RTF_RGBA8 at 8192^2 could be cut to an indexed/lower-bpp scheme or a smaller texture — halving the dimension to 4096 cuts VRAM 4x to 64 MiB; (2) since SRGB=False and bAutoGenerateMips=False already, the only way to materially reduce this 256 MiB is reducing RENDER_TEXTURE_SIZE or splitting the world into tiled render targets that are allocated lazily for occupied regions (most of the 8192^2 is empty, exactly as the analyst noted). Also worth verifying separately: OnWorldLoaded at cpp:394 does a full ClearRenderTarget2D over the entire 8192^2 target on every world load.

verdicts.corrections: Severity high is reasonable but the framing should shift. Two estimate corrections: (a) the per-batch cost for unrelated UI is NOT extra heap allocations — stock UE already does 2 allocs per new batch; the genuine added tax is the global trampoline detour + virtual dispatch through the replacement class + the IsCartograph capture/comparison, executed for every canvas batch process-wide. (b) The "risks leaks/double-free" sub-claim is effectively refuted: both deletion paths mirror stock UE and are guarded by Data=nullptr, so they are correct, not divergent bugs. Net: the real, defensible cost is a system-wide routing detour (every game/UI FCanvas batch goes through SML's ApplyCall hook dispatcher + Cartograph's item) to apply a scissor that is only needed for one canvas — that justifies high severity on overhead grounds, not on memory-safety grounds.
verdicts.extraInsight: Beyond per-batch cost, the global hook has correctness/robustness exposure the finding doesn't mention: the handler casts SortElement.RenderBatchArray.Last() to FCartographCanvasRenderItem* (cpp:342) for ANY canvas. Since the hook replaces allocation for all canvases, every batch element in the array is in fact a Cartograph item, so the cast is self-consistent — BUT it assumes RenderBatchArray only ever holds items produced by this hook. If any other SML mod hooks the same FCanvas::GetBatchedElements (SML hooks are chained — multiple AddHandlerBefore on one symbol, NativeHookManager.h:339-342), or if engine code elsewhere adds a stock FCanvasBatchedElementRenderItem to that array, the static_cast at cpp:342 is an unchecked downcast to the wrong type -> UB. Also note the hook is installed under `if (!WITH_EDITOR)` (cpp:304) with no Unsubscribe on module shutdown visible here, so the global patch persists for process lifetime. The cheap fix consistent with the finding: gate the handler body on `ClassInstance == UCartographGameInstanceModule::Instance->CurrentCanvas` and fall through to the original (Scope leaves default) for all other canvases, eliminating the system-wide tax and the cross-mod cast hazard in one change.

findings.title: Unchecked *TMap::Find() deref on the slice/timeout/rejoin race is the concrete #9 join crash
findings.mechanism: ServerRequestInitialBuildingData_Implementation dereferences *InitialBuildingDataToSendPerPlayer.Find(PlayerController) at RCO.cpp:65 (Finished), :73 (per-slice loop), and :87 (timeout lambda) with NO null check. TMap::Find returns nullptr when the entry is absent; dereferencing it reads/writes through a null FInitialBuildingDataToSend* -> immediate access violation on the server game thread (crashes the whole dedicated server, matching #9 'occasionally crashes when players attempt to join'). The entry can be absent at any of these sites via three real races: (1) TIMEOUT vs SLICE: the per-slice SetTimer at RCO.cpp:83-90 arms a 10s one-shot that Frees the buffer and Removes the entry. The protocol is strictly ping-pong: server sends slice -> client ClientReceiveInitialBuildingData -> client calls ServerRequestInitialBuildingData(Normal) -> server sends next slice. With a large factory the buffer can be tens of MB across thousands of slices (see overflow finding); a single RTT/packet-delay or a long client-side InitialBuildableDeserialize stall exceeding 10s fires the timeout, removes the entry, then the next Normal request arrives and hits *Find()==nullptr at :73. (2) FINISHED vs TIMEOUT double-removal: if Finished (client got last slice) and the timeout race each other, whichever runs second derefs a nullptr at :65/:87 (and double-frees, see below). (3) REJOIN/RESPAWN re-request: LambdaAfterCloseRespawnUI (GameInstanceModule.cpp:284-296) re-issues ServerRequestInitialBuildingData(Initial) on every respawn/UI-close; a stale in-flight Normal from a prior session, or two Initial phases interleaving, leaves the loop tail at :73 operating on an entry that a concurrent timeout already removed. There is also no HasAuthority/validity guard and PlayerController is used as a raw TMap key with no cleanup on logout, so a disconnect mid-transfer leaves a dangling-key entry and the timeout lambda captures a raw PlayerController by value that may be destroyed.
findings.fixDirection: Replace every `*Find()` with a checked `if (auto* Data = Find(PC); Data)` else CARTO_LOG_WARNING+return; key transfers by a stable PlayerState/NetId not raw APlayerController*; add a logout hook (OnLogout/EndPlay) to Free+Remove the entry; make the timeout reset per received-ack (sliding window) rather than a fixed 10s; guard re-entrant Initial by discarding/replacing any existing in-flight transfer for that player atomically.

findings.title: FBufferWriter stored-by-value in a TMap: broken move => double-free and dangling writer pointer when a 2nd player joins
findings.mechanism: FInitialBuildingDataToSend holds FBufferWriter InitialBuildingData by value (RCO.h:15) inside TMap<APlayerController*, FInitialBuildingDataToSend> (RCO.h:88). FBufferWriter has no user move ctor, so it is trivially/member-wise moved/copied: the raw `Writer` heap pointer (allocated via FMemory with EBufferWriterFlags::AllowResize) is SHALLOW-copied. The code comment at RCO.cpp:40 explicitly admits this ('FBufferWriter doesn't handle moving properly, don't TakeOwnership and free manually'). Two corruption paths follow: (A) TMap REHASH on growth: when a 2nd player joins, InitialBuildingDataToSendPerPlayer.Add (RCO.cpp:51) grows the sparse-array/hash and RELOCATES existing elements, member-wise moving each FBufferWriter. The first player's in-flight transfer is now reading/Memcpy'ing through a writer pointer that was bit-copied during relocation; because the type owns a raw pointer with no move semantics, you get aliasing and, on the source element's destruction, a free of a pointer the live copy still uses -> use-after-free in the Memcpy at RCO.cpp:78. (B) DOUBLE-FREE of GetWriterData(): the buffer is FMemory::Free'd manually in three places — Finished (RCO.cpp:67), timeout lambda (RCO.cpp:88), and (because FBufferWriter was constructed with raw ptr and NOT TakeOwnership, its destructor does not free, but the moved-from temporary `Archive` at RCO.cpp:48-52 still points at the same buffer). std::move(Archive) at RCO.cpp:52 leaves `Archive` aliasing the same Writer; if Finished and timeout both run (race), Free is called twice on the same address -> heap corruption/crash. Net effect on a busy dedicated server: the more players, the more rehash relocations and the higher the crash probability — directly explains why #9 is intermittent and join-triggered.
findings.fixDirection: Stop storing FBufferWriter by value. Serialize into a TArray<uint8> (which has correct move semantics and RAII) and store that — eliminates manual FMemory::Free entirely and all double-free/rehash-relocation hazards. Or heap-allocate the per-player state (TUniquePtr<FInitialBuildingDataToSend>) so the TMap moves a pointer, never the writer. Centralize teardown in one RAII destructor; never Free from multiple call sites.

findings.title: Slices computed from the moved-from Archive => wrong/zero slice count, off-by-one and stuck transfers
findings.mechanism: In the designated-initializer at RCO.cpp:51-55, `.InitialBuildingData = std::move(Archive)` is sequenced BEFORE `.Slices = Archive.TotalSize() / BuildingDataBufferMaxSize + 1` (aggregate init evaluates initializers left-to-right). So Slices is read from `Archive` AFTER it was moved-from. Given the broken move (previous finding), the moved-from Archive's TotalSize() is unreliable — it may still read the old size (because move is a shallow copy, so this particular bug is currently masked), but it is undefined-by-contract and a correct move fix would silently set Slices wrong. Independently, the slice math is off: TotalSize/Max + 1 over-counts by one whenever TotalSize is an exact multiple of Max (e.g. TotalSize=2047 -> Slices=2, but only 1 full slice exists; the extra slice copies Size=Min(2047, TotalSize - 1*2047)=0 bytes). The client's completion check ReceivedSliceCount==TotalSliceCount (RCO.cpp:103) then expects one more slice than the server's data warrants only when the server actually loops that many times — but the server stops based on client acks, so an over-counted Slices makes the client wait for a slice the server's i-loop will send as a 0-byte buffer, adding a wasted RTT; a mismatch from the move-bug interaction can make completion never trigger -> client stuck on loading -> 10s server timeout -> entry removed -> next ack null-derefs (ties to crash finding).
findings.fixDirection: Capture TotalSize into a local BEFORE the move; compute Slices = (TotalSize + Max - 1) / Max (ceil-div, no off-by-one); store TotalSize alongside and drive completion by bytes-received >= TotalSize rather than fragile slice-count equality.

findings.title: int64 Slices truncated to int16 TotalSliceCount: mega-factories silently overflow and the client never completes
findings.mechanism: Slices is int64_t (RCO.h:16) but is passed to ClientReceiveInitialBuildingData whose TotalSliceCount param is int16 (RCO.h:76, cpp:79) and ReceivedSliceCount is int16 (RCO.h:91). int16 max is 32767. Each slice carries BuildingDataBufferMaxSize=65535/32=2047 bytes (RCO.h:33). The buffer is the FULL serialized CurrentBuildingData. Overflow occurs at TotalSize ~= 32767*2047 = 67.07 MB. With a measured per-FBuildingData footprint on this byte-granular FBufferWriter (4B class hash + ~8B packed location + ~7B compressed rotator + ~1B extra-index, ~20B typical for a normal building per CartographDataStructure.cpp:118-206), that is ~3.35M buildings (and as low as ~1.68M for 40B spline/wire-heavy elements). At that size TotalSliceCount wraps to negative; ReceivedSliceCount (counting up positively) can never equal a negative target, so IsLast is never true (RCO.cpp:103), the client is stuck at the loading screen forever, the 10s server timeout fires and frees the per-player buffer, and the next client ack null-derefs (ties to crash finding). Also InitializeProgress = ReceivedSliceCount/TotalSliceCount (RCO.cpp:101) divides by a negative -> bogus/NaN progress bar. Even below overflow, ~3M slices × 1 RTT ping-pong is a multi-minute serial transfer.
findings.fixDirection: Use int32 (or int64) end-to-end for slice counts and the received counter; or eliminate slice-count from the wire entirely and send a one-time uint32 TotalByteSize, completing on bytes-received>=TotalSize. Increase slice payload (e.g. send near the 64KB reliable-bunch limit per slice) to cut the ping-pong RTT count by ~30x.

findings.title: Server serializes ENTIRE CurrentBuildingData synchronously on the game thread per joining player => multi-MB alloc + hitch on every Initial
findings.mechanism: On EInitialDataSendPhase::Initial the server does `Archive << CurrentBuildingData` in one synchronous call on the game thread (RCO.cpp:48), allocating a resizable FBufferWriter that grows to the full factory size (tens of MB for large saves) in a single burst, with repeated geometric reallocations during AllowResize growth (each realloc memcpy's the whole buffer so far -> O(N) extra copies, ~2x-3x transient peak). This runs once per Initial phase, i.e. once per join AND again on every respawn/UI-close (GameInstanceModule.cpp:284-296), producing a game-thread hitch and a large transient allocation each time. On a dedicated server with multiple players joining/respawning around the same time, these allocations stack (one full copy per concurrent transfer, each ~67MB-class for a mega-factory) and are never shared, multiplying server memory and stalling the simulation tick that all players share.
findings.fixDirection: Serialize the snapshot ONCE into a shared, ref-counted immutable byte blob (TSharedRef<TArray<uint8>>) regenerated only on actual data change; have all in-flight player transfers index into the same blob (zero per-player copies). Pre-reserve the writer to a size estimate to avoid resize memcpys. Optionally build the blob on a worker thread since CurrentBuildingData is only appended on the game thread.

findings.title: FBuildingDataBuffer::NetSerialize always sends the full 2047-byte buffer regardless of actual Size
findings.mechanism: FBuildingDataBuffer is a fixed uint8 Data[2047] (RCO.h:41) and NetSerialize unconditionally Ar.Serialize(Data, BuildingDataBufferMaxSize) = 2047 bytes (RCO.cpp:17), ignoring the separately-replicated `Size`. Every slice therefore transmits a full 2047-byte bunch even when Size<2047 — always true for the final slice, and for the over-counted 0-byte spurious slice. More importantly it means each slice is a fixed 2047B reliable RPC: a mega-factory (~67MB) needs ~33k such RPCs, each gated by a full client->server->client RTT (the protocol is strict ping-pong, RCO.cpp:79 then :110-111), so transfer time is ~33k×RTT (minutes at 30-50ms RTT) and the fixed timeout (10s) cannot bound this. It also wastes bandwidth on the tail and prevents adapting slice size to the reliable-bunch MTU.
findings.fixDirection: Serialize only `Size` bytes (write Size first, then Serialize(Data, Size)); send a window of N slices per ack (or stream multiple bunches before waiting) to amortize RTT; size each slice toward the reliable-bunch limit (~tens of KB) to cut slice count ~30x.

findings.title: ClientUpdateBuildingData is NetMulticast Reliable fired per build event => reliable-channel saturation during mass building
findings.mechanism: ACartographModSubsystem::ClientUpdateBuildingData is UFUNCTION(NetMulticast, Reliable) (ModSubsystem.h:32) and is invoked once per redraw/build batch from ExecuteRedrawMapCoroutine (GameInstanceModule.cpp:927) carrying full TArray<FBuildingData> add/remove payloads. Reliable multicasts are queued on every client's connection and MUST be delivered in order; during mass operations (blueprint stamping, dismantling a large area, Ctrl-drag belts/foundations) the server emits a flood of reliable multicasts, each replicating FBuildingData arrays to ALL clients. This (a) saturates each client's reliable channel, (b) grows the per-connection reliable bunch queue unboundedly if a client is slow, which can overflow/disconnect, and (c) on a dedicated server multiplies cost by player count. Reliable+multicast+high-frequency+large-payload is the textbook recipe for the post-1.2 'severe lag spikes' and 'belt placement triggers crash' in #14 on multiplayer, and a slow/late-joining client whose reliable queue backs up while ALSO receiving the slice transfer compounds the #9 join instability.
findings.fixDirection: Coalesce build deltas server-side into a periodic (e.g. 0.5-1s) batched update instead of per-event; consider Unreliable multicast with a periodic reliable reconciliation snapshot (sequence-numbered) so a dropped delta self-heals rather than blocking the reliable queue; cap per-message payload and rate-limit; skip the multicast entirely for players still in the Initial transfer phase to avoid stacking with the slice stream.

verdicts.corrections: One sub-claim is inaccurate: the "InitialBuildableDeserialize stall exceeding 10s delays the Normal ack" pathway does NOT hold as stated. Deserialize runs only on the LAST slice (CartographRemoteCallObject.cpp:104-108), not per slice, and InitialBuildableDeserialize is a latent UE5Coro coroutine (returns/suspends immediately at the first `co_await Budget` on line 146), so line 110 sends the Finished ack right away rather than after deserialize completes. Thus a deserialize stall never delays a mid-transfer Normal ack. The correct trigger for race (1) is plain network RTT / packet retransmit / general client game-thread stall exceeding the timeout, not the deserialize coroutine. Also a precision note: the same TimerHandle is re-armed every slice (:83 with the handle stored in the entry), so the 10s is a per-slice idle timeout, not a whole-transfer budget — this makes the timeout-vs-slice race require a single round-trip stall >10s (somewhat narrower than "fixed 10s independent of factory size" implies, though :33 is indeed a fixed constant). Severity remains critical; the core null-deref-on-absent-entry mechanism is fully confirmed.
verdicts.extraInsight: Two additional co-located bugs confirmed while verifying: (1) int16 slice-count overflow. Slices is computed/stored as int64_t (header:16, .cpp:53) but passed to ClientReceiveInitialBuildingData as int16 TotalSliceCount (.cpp:79, header:76) and counted with int16 ReceivedSliceCount (header:91). With BuildingDataBufferMaxSize = 65535/32 = 2047 bytes, int16 max 32767 slices => ~67 MB of serialized CurrentBuildingData overflows TotalSliceCount to negative, so ReceivedSliceCount==TotalSliceCount (line 103 IsLast) can never match (or matches wrongly) => transfer never finishes / InitializeProgress (line 101) divides by a negative => the per-slice timeout then fires and yields exactly the same null-deref crash. Large factories on dedicated servers are the #9 population, so this overflow is a strong amplifier of the same crash. (2) The Finished path can double-free: :67 frees GetWriterData() then :68 removes; the timeout lambda at :88 frees again — if both fire (race 2) it is a null-deref AND/OR double-free. (3) FBufferWriter with EBufferWriterFlags::AllowResize is std::move'd into the struct (.cpp:42,51-55) but the comment at :40 notes FBufferWriter "doesn't handle moving properly," and the code manually frees GetWriterData() — a fragile ownership pattern that compounds the double-free risk. Recommended fix is trivial and high-value: replace all three `*Find()` with a checked `if (auto* P = Find(...))` guard, add a Logout/EndPlay handler to Free+Remove the entry, widen slice counts to int32, and gate the respawn re-request on no in-flight transfer.

verdicts.corrections:
Severity should be downgraded from "critical" to roughly "low/medium." The headline mechanisms are wrong: (1) no destructor double-free, because the buffer is non-owning (AllowResize, not TakeOwnership => bFreeOnClose==false), so the shallow-copy "broken move" is harmless and is in fact why .Slices reads correctly; (2) no rehash-driven UAF, because the RCO and its map are per-PlayerController (Within=FGPlayerController), so the map holds at most one entry and a 2nd player never touches another player's map; (3) no concurrent or sequential double-free, because the game thread is single-threaded and Finished ClearTimer's the one-shot timeout before freeing, and both exit paths Remove the entry. None of these explains issue #9 the way claimed.</corrections>
<extraInsight>There IS a real but different defect in the same code: every `*InitialBuildingDataToSendPerPlayer.Find(PlayerController)` (cpp:65, cpp:73, cpp:87) dereferences Find's result with NO null check. If the 10s timeout (cpp:33) fires — plausible on a laggy join or a very large factory, since each ~2047-byte slice (BuildingDataBufferMaxSize=65535/32=2047, h:33) requires a full client->server round-trip at cpp:110 — the entry is Free'd and Removed (cpp:88-89); any subsequent in-flight slice RPC or a late Finished then does `*Find(...)` on a missing key => NULL-POINTER DEREFERENCE crash (not a double-free/heap-corruption). That is a genuine join-time crash path consistent with issue #9, but the mechanism is a null deref after timeout, not move/rehash/double-free. Secondary: the manual-free design is fragile (relies on AllowResize-without-TakeOwnership and on FBufferWriter's exact Realloc behavior); a cleaner fix is to store the serialized bytes in a TArray<uint8> (TakeOwnership/owning RAII) and drop all manual FMemory::Free, plus add null checks on every Find.</extraInsight>
</invoke>
